summary: Antoine Bazin was a sinologist who studied at the Collège de France under Stanislas Julien from circa 1832 to 1838. In 1852, he served as Secrétaire-adjoint of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École du Louvre and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at the BnF, EFEO, INALCO, and ENFOM.

Antoine Grégoire was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Liège, Leipzig, Munich, and Paris under Brugmann, Sievers, Hirt, Kuhn, Bréal, Henry, and Meillet. He later served as professor at Liège (1905–1942) and taught at ULB (1936–1945).
Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Marie Tabard was an Indologist and historian. He taught mathematics, physics, and chemistry at St. Joseph's University (1891–1924), founded The Mythic Society in 1909, and served as its president in 1910.

Antoine Meillet was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand de Saussure and Abel Bergaigne, and he later taught numerous prominent scholars, including Joseph Vendryes, Georges Dumézil, and Louis Renou.

Antoine Mosac was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Superior of the Jesuit Mission of Chandernagore in 1742 and as Superior of the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1775 to 1777.
Antoine-Gaspard Bellin was an Indologist who earned his Dr.iuris at the University of Lyon by 1839. He served as a civil judge and librarian at the Tribunal civil de Lyon from circa 1851 to 1885.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian specialist. He held chairs in Arabic (1795) and Persian (1806) at INALCO, served as president of the Société Asiatique (1822–1829, 1832–1834), and taught Franz Bopp and Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat.

Antoine-Jean Saint-Martin studied at the Collège des Quatre-Nations and INALCO under Silvestre de Sacy. Active in linguistics and history, he co-founded the Société Asiatique, directed the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1824), and held posts at the Imprimerie Nationale and foreign ministry.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist and colonel in the East India Company. He studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he founded the Société Asiatique, held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1815–1832), and taught Franz Bopp and Eugène Burnouf.

Anton Boller was an Austrian linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna. He later taught there as Dozent and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics from 1845 onward and became a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1828–1831). He later lectured there on oriental and modern languages (1849–1852) and worked at the Royal Danish Library.

id: P:Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun
summary: Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun, an Indologist, studied at the Theresian Military Academy. He directed the Madras Military Institution (1807), served as Secretary of Sanskrit College (1827–1835), and was affiliated with the Oriental Translation Fund.
Anton Gerard van Hamel was a linguist who studied at the Barlaeus Gymnasium from circa 1898 to 1904. He held a post at Utrecht University from 1923 to 1945, where he taught Jan Gonda.

Anton Kogan, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the Russian State University for the Humanities from 1992 to 1997. In 2000, he became a Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Anton Scherer studied at the University of Munich under Gustav Herbig, Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, and Ferdinand Sommer. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Munich, held a professorship at Würzburg (1948–1951), and was a professor at Heidelberg (1951–1969).

Anton Schiefner studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin. An expert in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, he held multiple leadership posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, directed the Peter the Great Museum, and taught classical languages.

Anton Walter Florus Gueth was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a docent at Taisho University in 1921 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1922. His students included Nyanaponika Thera and Acharya Buddharakkhita.
